marks.gloss_en: Rav Nachman: if he is a Torah scholar, he need not [recite the Shema on his bed]
Torah was given to Israel only by means of suffering
Torah [through suffering] -- from Ps 94:12: 'happy is the man whom You afflict, Lord, and teach from Your Torah'

Eretz Yisrael [through suffering] -- from Deut 8:5 'as a man chastens his son, the Lord your God chastens you', followed by 8:7 'for the Lord your God brings you to a good land' (the derivation runs on the juxtaposition)
the World-to-Come [through suffering] -- from Prov 6:23: 'the mitzva is a lamp and Torah is light, and the reproofs of instruction are the way of life'
one who engages in Torah and in acts of kindness -- all his sins are forgiven
one should always incite his good inclination against his evil inclination -- as it is said, 'tremble, and do not sin'
'tablets' -- these are the ten commandments

מה שן ועין שהן אחד מאבריו של אדם עבד יוצא בהן לחירות, יסורין שממרקין כל גופו של אדם על אחת כמה וכמה -- if losing one limb wins a slave his freedom, afflictions that scour the whole body surely win a man release from his sins

נאמר ברית במלח (ולא תשבית מלח ברית, Lev 2:13) ונאמר ברית ביסורין (אלה דברי הברית, Deut 28:69): as the salt-covenant's salt sweetens the meat, the affliction-covenant's afflictions scour away all a man's sins
שנאמר רוממות אל בגרונם וחרב פיפיות בידם (Ps 149:6)

מאי משמע? מרישא דענינא: the preceding verse reads יעלזו חסידים בכבוד ירננו על משכבותם (Ps 149:5) -- praise upon their beds is the Shema -- וכתיב בתריה the sword; so the sword-verse is about the Shema on the bed (Mar Zutra, ואיתימא Rav Ashi)
one who reads the Shema on his bed is as if he holds a double-edged sword in his hand
שנאמר ובני רשף יגביהו עוף (Job 5:7), with עוף read as Torah and רשף as demons
one who reads the Shema on his bed -- demons keep away from him
שנאמר ובני רשף יגביהו עוף (Job 5:7), with עוף read as Torah and רשף as afflictions
one who engages in Torah -- afflictions keep away from him
שנאמר נאלמתי דומיה החשיתי מטוב וכאבי נעכר (Ps 39:3) -- silent from 'good', i.e. from Torah, and his pain is troubled
R' Yochanan's reading of the verse: one who could engage in Torah and does not -- the Holy One brings ugly, troubling afflictions upon him
שנאמר כי לקח טוב נתתי לכם תורתי אל תעזבו (Prov 4:2) -- a 'good purchase', praised by the seller
unlike flesh and blood, where the seller grieves and the buyer rejoices, the Holy One gave the Torah to Israel and rejoiced
שנאמר נחפשה דרכינו ונחקרה ונשובה עד ה' (Lam 3:40)
שנאמר אשרי הגבר אשר תיסרנו יה ומתורתך תלמדנו (Ps 94:12)
if a person sees afflictions coming upon him, he should examine his deeds
שנאמר כי את אשר יאהב ה' יוכיח (Prov 3:12)
if he attributed them so and found nothing, it is known that they are afflictions of love
שנאמר וה' חפץ דכאו החלי (Isa 53:10)
whomever the Holy One delights in, He crushes with afflictions
יראה זרע יאריך ימים -- the continuation of Isa 53:10
שנאמר וחפץ ה' בידו יצלח (Isa 53:10)
if he accepted them, his reward: 'he shall see offspring, he shall lengthen his days'
שנאמר אשרי הגבר אשר תיסרנו יה ומתורתך תלמדנו (Ps 94:12) -- afflictions of love leave him able to be taught from Your Torah
afflictions of love are those that involve no neglect of Torah study

אלא מה תלמוד לומר ומתורתך תלמדנו -- אל תקרי תלמדנו אלא תלמדנו: the verse does not condition afflictions of love on continued study; it says 'THIS you teach us from Your Torah' -- that afflictions atone (the kal vachomer at 5a.18)
read not 'You teach him' but 'You teach us': this matter -- that afflictions atone -- You teach us from Your Torah
שנאמר ברוך אלהים אשר לא הסיר תפלתי וחסדו מאתי (Ps 66:20)
afflictions of love are those that involve no neglect of prayer
שנאמר כי את אשר יאהב ה' יוכיח (Prov 3:12) -- rebuke of the beloved, with no condition attached
both -- even afflictions that interrupt Torah study and even those that interrupt prayer -- are afflictions of love
entertained: perhaps this holds even if he did not accept the afflictions with love
